Remember the order of a plot's components

Source: R/components.R
steps.Rd

Wrap the code that makes a plot in `steps()` to store the order of its `+` components inside the plot. The result is a normal ggplot (you can print, save and `readRDS()` it), and [ggppt()] / [ggtex()] can later reveal any of its components with `scope = "all"` or `scope = "all_but_theme"`.

Usage

steps(plot)

Arguments

plot

The code that makes the plot, e.g. `ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() + labs(title = "A")`.

Value

The plot, with the component order stored as an attribute.

Details

Only needed for these two scopes. With the default `scope = "layers"`, any saved ggplot works without `steps()`.

Examples

library(ggplot2)
p <- steps(
  ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
    geom_point() +                                  # 1
    labs(title = "Fuel use") +                      # 2
    theme_minimal() +                               # 3
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x)     # 4
)
plot_components(p)
#>  component                                   all all_but_theme layers
#>  geom_point()                                1   1             1     
#>  labs(title = "Fuel use")                    2   2             -     
#>  theme_minimal()                             3   -             -     
#>  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) 4   3             2
